notes.title: Later evidence for river and marketplace rights
notes.body: Plasencia's 1589 account reports that some Tagalog chiefs claimed particular fisheries and market stretches and that access could carry obligations. It is evidence for possible local and differentiated claims, not a contemporaneous record of a uniform port authority or the precise early-1520s marker dispute between Maynila and the far bank.

notes.title: Regional exchange and earlier records
notes.body: Pires's early-sixteenth-century commercial intelligence supports Luzon's participation in regional trade; the tenth-century Laguna Copperplate Inscription demonstrates much earlier written transactions and debt relations. Neither source documents the wooden stake, the keeper's cord and marks, the boat owners' meeting, a particular ferry tariff, or the way this fictional community recorded consent.

links.label: Clavé and Griffiths on the Laguna Copperplate Inscription (2022)

notes.title: Competing households and a bounded repair
notes.body: The displaced channel stake, damaged fish basket, keeper's hearing, Dala and Pawi's repaired net frame, the witnessed sounding and the boat owners' competing demands are invented. A messenger associated with Lakandula's household does not bind that house to the proposed arrangement, and the repaired passage creates no kingdom-wide settlement, new tax or hereditary command. The earlier hall agreement remains conditional, and Ache must still negotiate work and payment with people who can refuse.
